chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Najran, I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Najran.

key_terms.أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, a well-known narrator
key_terms.رضي الله عنه: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific for a narrator
key_terms.عبد الرحمن بن أبي نجران: Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Najran, a prominent narrator
key_terms.محمد بن الحسن: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key scholar in the chain
key_terms.محمد بن الحسن الصفار: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, known as the Saffar

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of transmission for narrations from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Najran in this book?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq explicitly links the narrations of Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Najran to the prominent scholar Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, a key figure in the Kufan school of hadith. This specific chain highlights the scholarly network of the late 3rd/early 4th century Hijri, emphasizing the reliability of Abdur Rahman through his connection to the 'Two Muhammads' (al-Saffar and al-Hasan), thereby reinforcing the authenticity of the transmitted jurisprudence.
